a.d: In Teresina, a “churrasco” is a family event: meat on skewers, farofa, vinaigrette and cold drinks. Guests often bring something. Use “Posso ajudar?” and “O que você traz?”. False friend: “carne” is meat, while “carne de sol” is sun-dried meat.

a.d: In Palmas, pharmacies are everywhere and the “farmacêutico” can recommend simple remedies. Say “Estou com dor de cabeça” or “Estou resfriado”. Prescription drugs need a “receita”. False friend: “constipado” does not mean constipated here; it is a Portuguese (Portugal) word for a cold.

a.d: In Santa Maria, a typical home has “sofá”, “mesa”, “cadeira”, “cama”, “geladeira” and “fogão”. Use prepositions of place: “em cima de” (on top of), “embaixo de” (under), “ao lado de” (next to). False friend: “geladeira” is fridge; “refrigerador” is formal.

a.d: In Uberlândia, you can go to a “clínica” or “posto de saúde”. The doctor asks “O que o senhor está sentindo?”. Answer with “Estou com…”. Use “dói” for pain: “Dói aqui”. False friend: “médico” means doctor, “medicina” medicine as a field; the pill is “remédio”.

a.d: In Caxias do Sul, in the south, winters can be cold. Ask “Como está o tempo?” or “Que tempo faz?”. Use “Está” + adjective: “Está frio, está chovendo, está ensolarado”. False friend: “tempo” means both time and weather.
